newsitem.title: UK: UK Insurance IT spend to rise as competition grows.
newsitem.headline: UK Insurance IT spend to rise as competition grows.

text.p: The British insurance industry is likely to be increasingly fragmented and competitive in the next century with products sold through a host of outlets -- retailers, banks, building societies, direct writers and brokers according to strategic consultants, Datamonitor.

According to a new report "IT in UK Personal General Insurance' customers will also have greater choice how they pay for insurance with telephone, the Internet, shops, banks and high street kiosks all likely to provide cover.
One of the dynamos for growth over the next few years will be consolidation of the market, leading to major companies merging and integrating their systems.
Underwriters are also likely to make significant investments in core systems to enable sophisticated underwriting strategies and streamline policy and claims processing, according to Datamonitor.
As a result, Datamonitor forecasts that UK underwriters will be spending over one billion stg on IT by 2001, up from 758 million stg in 1996, an annual growth rate of eight percent.
